messages:
maria.support: FYI incoming customer escalation — multiple customers in eu-north reporting 5xx/timeouts on /v1/generate since ~08:12 UTC. Error rate +80% vs baseline. Repro steps and logs below.

maria.support: sample from customer A: HTTP 502 body: "upstream read timeout". They sent a curl that times out consistently for longer prompts.

maria.support: repro curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"model":"redwood-1.5","prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024}' -v --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 30```

sam.net: I see spike in SYN retransmits between eu-north1 and our eu-central backbone at 08:10. Net metrics show microbursts and ~2.5% packet loss on some inter-AZ paths. Correlates with customer reports.

jordan.infra: Which host pools are affected? Any particular gateway/edge?

sam.net: Affected: hostpool-rua-eun-1 (eu-north AZs a/b). Edge gateways eu-north-gw-1/2 showing increased retransmit counters. BGP flaps observed to carrier-3 peering at 08:09-08:18.

irene.sre: Can we confirm if routing fallback to eu-central is working? We have an active routing policy but need to ensure no sticky sessions.

jordan.infra: Rolling traffic to eu-central now for new sessions (policy: latency-first). Setting route override for tenant tags with high error rates.

deploy-bot: route-override applied for tenant-tag:customer-escalations -> target-region:europe-central at 08:26 UTC (initiated by jordan.infra).

maria.support: Customer A confirms reduced errors after ~08:28, but some long live streams still see 503s. They reported auth retries too (token reauth failures) — could be side effect of retransmits.

tim.oncall: Looking at API gateway logs: surge of 502s where upstream connection reset by peer; connection latencies to backend increased from 25ms to 180ms during window. Also seeing increased TLS handshake retries.

sam.net: Reached out to carrier-3 NOC — they report a multipath forwarding imbalance on peering fabric causing out-of-order packets and drops. They will apply microconfig to disable ECMP across two flaps and push a fix; ETA 40m.

provider-alert-bot: carrier-3 status update: "We observed an intermittent forwarding anomaly between our FRA and OSL POPs due to hardware queue contention; mitigation in-progress" - 08:35 UTC.

alex.account: Notifying top impacted customers and issuing incident advisory. Putting temporary credits on affected invoices for the window.

irene.sre: For longer-term, we should consider adding per-connection packet-loss thresholds to trigger automatic cross-region session migration for streaming endpoints. Filing ticket: INF-1258.

jordan.infra: Created INF-1258 and linked this thread. Also enabling aggressive TCP keepalive and reducing idle timeouts for gateway-proxy connections as a short-term tweak. Will monitor.

maria.support: Customer B still seeing intermittent 504s on embedded SDKs that reuse connections. Any plan for connection draining or forcing reconnects?

tim.oncall: Pushing proxy config to drop long-reused connections to force reconnects to new routed path for affected hostpool. Will target 10% of connections first as canary.

deploy-bot: proxy-config rollout started (canary 10%) - 08:56 UTC by tim.oncall.

maria.support: Customer B confirms improvement after 09:05 UTC. Error rates back down to near-baseline by 09:12.

sam.net: Carrier-3 reports mitigation applied at 09:14; packet-loss returned to normal levels. Continual watch for 30m.

irene.sre: Marking incident brief: brief cause = carrier multipath imbalance causing packet loss/out-of-order; impact = elevated 5xx and timeouts for eu-north hosted inference, mainly streaming/long requests and connection-reuse flows; mitigations = traffic reroute to eu-central, proxy reconnects, carrier config applied.

maria.support: I'll follow up with affected customers (tickets updated) and include timeline + credits. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
